title: 元知识详解：网络科学 — Day 13

questions.question: 一个团队信息流转很慢。按小世界网络的原理，哪种改动最可能用最小成本大幅缩短信息传递的路径？
options: 把全员的联系彻底打散重新随机分配，让每个人和任意部门都有同样多的联系
在几个原本不相往来的部门之间建立两三条跨部门协作关系，不必频繁联系
增加全员例会的频率，让所有信息都集中在会上同步，减少私下的点对点传递
让每个人都和本部门所有同事保持更密切的日常沟通，把邻里关系织得更紧
questions.explanation: Watts 与 Strogatz 的模型显示，在邻里紧密的网络里只要加入极少量跨圈捷径，平均距离就会骤降，同时保留邻里结构。全部打散成随机网络虽然路径也短，却丢掉了邻里紧密度；问题不在沟通太少，而在缺少几条跨部门的桥。
questions.question_en: Information moves slowly through a team. Based on small-world network principles, which change is most likely to sharply shorten information paths at the lowest cost?
options_en: Scramble everyone's connections at random so each person is equally linked to every department
Set up two or three working ties between departments that don't normally talk — no need for frequent contact
Hold all-hands meetings more often so all information is synced there rather than passed person to person
Have everyone communicate more closely with all colleagues in their own department, tightening local ties
questions.explanation_en: Watts and Strogatz showed that adding just a few long-range shortcuts to a highly clustered network collapses the average path length while keeping local clustering. Fully randomizing also gives short paths but destroys the local structure. The problem isn't too little communication; it's missing a few cross-group bridges.

questions.question: 关于无标度网络（少数枢纽连接极多、大多数节点连接很少）的稳健性，下列哪种说法正确？
options: 由于大多数节点都很脆弱，随机损坏 5% 的节点就足以让无标度网络失去连通性
随机损坏一部分节点几乎没影响，但专门打掉连接最多的少数枢纽会让全网近乎瘫痪
无论随机损坏还是定向攻击，影响都取决于损坏节点的总数，与挑哪些节点无关
因为枢纽之间有大量冗余连接，即使枢纽被精准打掉，网络也能靠其余节点维持连通
questions.explanation: 绝大多数节点连接很少，随机坏掉的几乎总是这些不重要的节点，所以随机故障影响很小；而连通性高度依赖少数枢纽，定向打掉它们网络就会崩溃。枢纽既是稳健的来源也是最大的弱点，所以「挑哪些节点无关」恰好说反了。
questions.question_en: Regarding the robustness of scale-free networks (a few hubs with huge numbers of links, most nodes with very few), which statement is correct?
options_en: Since most nodes are fragile, randomly removing just 5% of nodes is enough to break a scale-free network apart
Randomly knocking out some nodes barely matters, but deliberately taking out the few biggest hubs nearly cripples the network
Random failure and targeted attack do the same damage; what matters is how many nodes fail, not which ones
Because hubs are heavily interconnected, the network stays connected through other nodes even if hubs are targeted
questions.explanation_en: Most nodes have few links, so random failures almost always hit unimportant nodes and do little harm. But connectivity depends heavily on a handful of hubs, so a targeted attack on them collapses the network. Hubs are both the source of robustness and the biggest weakness, so "which nodes doesn't matter" gets it backwards.

questions.question: 公司准备裁员，名单上有一位职位不高、KPI 也不亮眼的跨部门协调员。用「中介中心性」的视角，应该先看什么？
options: 这个人的直接产出与同级员工相比排在什么位置，产出靠后的就可以先裁
有多少跨部门之间的信息和合作路径必须经过这个人，他走后哪些流会断
这个人在公司里认识的同事总数有多少，人脉越广的员工越不应该被裁掉
这个人在组织架构图上离高管有几级，离决策层越近的节点权力越大越难替代
questions.explanation: 中介中心性衡量的是有多少条最短路径必须穿过某个节点，桥接两个群体的人不必朋友最多，却垄断了跨群体的信息流。只看人脉总数是把度数和中介性混为一谈；这类协调者的价值常常要等他离开、项目周期拉长后才显现。
questions.question_en: A company is planning layoffs, and the list includes a cross-team coordinator with a modest title and unimpressive KPIs. From a betweenness-centrality perspective, what should you look at first?
options_en: How this person's direct output ranks against peers at the same level, cutting the lowest performers first
How many cross-team information and collaboration paths run through this person, and which would break if they left
How many colleagues this person knows in total — the wider someone's network, the less they should be cut
How many levels this person sits below the executives, since nodes closer to leadership hold more power
questions.explanation_en: Betweenness centrality counts how many shortest paths must pass through a node. Someone bridging two groups needn't have the most contacts, yet controls the flow between them. Counting total contacts confuses degree with betweenness; a bridge's value often only shows after they leave and projects slow down.
